messages:
maria: putting up a short follow-up on shard reload/backoff behavior after the RFC. TL;DR: plan for a staggered, observable swap that avoids global OOMs and keeps KV cache correctness.

alex: interested — can you sketch the sequence? we keep tripping over reload storms when a bad checkpoint hits.

maria: yep. proposed sequence: 1) publisher uploads new safetensors + manifest with version & checksum. 2) manifest is registered in registry service (atomic write). 3) loaders start a prefetch wave into a warm pool (limited concurrency). 4) router marks a canary percent of traffic to the new shards and verifies perf/health. 5) if canary passes, perform staggered atomic swap across shard groups with backoff between groups. 6) on failure, automatically rollback to previous manifest.

wei: couple important constraints: a) KV cache layout must be compatible or we must invalidate cache per-shard during swap. b) in-flight requests referencing old kv pages need to be handled — either finish on old memory or be retried against old model.

sam: +1. For (a) i'd rather invalidate per-shard and let requests repopulate than attempt cross-version reuse. Invalidates are cheaper than subtle correctness bugs.

maria: Agreed. Implementation notes: - warm pool: ephemeral GPU memory allocation that holds warm copies of new shards. don't touch production dispatch until canary ok. - per-shard swap is an atomic pointer update in the loader process (swap must be lock-free for readers). - we enforce a per-host max_parallel_shard_swaps to limit memory pressure.

alex: what about backoff when prefetch slows / disk throttles? We need a circuit-breaker.

wei: propose algorithm: exponential backoff + jitter per-shard-group with metrics trigger. Pseudoconfig: 
```json
{
  "reload": {
    "grace_period_ms": 30000,
    "max_parallel_shard_swaps": 2,
    "group_size": 8,
    "backoff_initial_ms": 500,
    "backoff_multiplier": 2,
    "backoff_max_ms": 60000,
    "health_check_window": 120000
  }
}
```
This keeps swaps small and widens the gap if the storage tier is saturated.

maria: add jitter to avoid synchronized waves across hosts. also expose metrics: `shard_reload.swap_attempt`, `shard_reload.swap_success`, `shard_reload.swap_fail` and `shard_reload.prefetch_latency_ms`. Alert on high failure rate or high prefetch latency.

sam: fallback plan for severe load: automatically route a small percent to a compat-quantized fallback model (smaller RAM footprint) until swap completes. We already support variant routing by policy, so reuse that.

alex: how to handle manifest version pinning for in-flight requests? if request references model@v1 and we swapped to v2, we should honor model@v1 until TTL expires.

maria: yes. policy: explicit pinning in the request wins. Default (un-pinned) traffic uses the latest stable manifest. Pinned requests get served by a pinned runtime slice. That implies we must retain old shards until GC window passes. config example: `pinned_ttl_ms` (default 5m).

wei: ops API: we need commands to force-swap / abort in-flight reloads. Sample: 
```
infractl model reload --model-id=my-llm --manifest=sha256:abcd --force
infractl model reload abort --op=reload-789
```
These show up in the audit log.

warmup-bot: warmup progress: prefetch 32/128 shards warm on host infra-03; avg prefetch latency 24ms; backoff engaged for group 3 (sleep 1.1s).

maria: outstanding design questions: - eviction vs warm pool sizing: prefer conservative warm pool so we don't balloon memory. - should we support differential KV compatibility map in the manifest? (i.e., mark which layers are binary-compatible). - canary sizing: default 5% but allow customer override.

sam: for differential KV map: useful for multi-format migration (e.g., float16->quant). but it complicates loader logic. maybe start without it and add later.

alex: agree — ship minimal: manifest+checksum+staggered swap+backoff+metrics. iterate on compatibility map if customers demand live in-place upgrades.

maria: i'll put this up as a short RFC follow-up doc with mocks and the operator commands. tagging @alex @wei @sam for review, will iterate on config names. thanks! :rocket:
